page_hint: Chapter 10, §5 Common Mistakes, bullet 'Using TP without budgeting its exchanges'
quoted_clause: Using TP without budgeting its exchanges. The same 490 GB takes ~18× longer at 25 GB/s than at 450 GB/s (490/25 ≈ 19.6 s vs 490/450 ≈ 1.09 s), but whether it binds depends on message shape, call count and exposed latency.
observed: The 490 GB quantity is the DP FP32 gradient all-reduce per-rank send volume from §10.3, not the TP activation exchange discussed in the bullet title. The TP decode example in the same chapter uses 70 MiB per rank per step, not 490 GB.
evidence: §10.3 DP: 'per-rank send volume is 2 × 245 ≈ 490 GB'. §10.3 TP: 'Across 160 calls ... each rank sends 70 MiB and receives 70 MiB in that one decode step.'
root_cause: A DP gradient number was reused in a TP common-mistake bullet without relabeling the communication object.
correction: Either replace the 490 GB example with the TP activation volume (e.g., 70 MiB per rank per decode step, or the per-layer 448 KiB ring send volume), or explicitly say 'the same 490 GB DP gradient all-reduce' and then return to TP per-layer exchanges.
acceptance_test: The TP bullet no longer implies that TP moves 490 GB per step; if 490 GB appears, it is explicitly identified as the DP gradient all-reduce, and the TP-specific byte budget is stated separately.

quoted_clause: cached prefixes and the live batch's pages draw on the same 640 GB KV pool, so reuse needs headroom
observed: 640 GB is the total HBM of an 8×H100 host, not the KV pool. The book's canonical KV budget is 436 GB after 140 GB weights and ~64 GB runtime/workspace.
evidence: Ch 11/12 repeatedly use '640 − 140 weights − ~64 runtime ≈ 436 GB' as the per-host KV budget.
root_cause: Host HBM and KV budget were conflated in the figure caption.
correction: Change to 'the same 640 GB HBM pool' or, more precisely, 'the same 436 GB KV budget'.
acceptance_test: No caption or prose calls the 640 GB host memory a 'KV pool'; if a KV pool is named, it uses the 436 GB canonical budget or an explicitly different assumption.

quoted_clause: the single-request residency check passes (164 GB < 640 GB), workload KV residency does not (§12.3), and one host's ~19.8K prefill tok/s is far short of the ~92K the 10 rps average demands, so memory passes and throughput opens.
observed: The sentence first states that workload KV residency does not pass, then concludes that memory passes. But §12.3 defines the memory gate as the workload KV residency check, not the single-request check.
evidence: §12.3: 'The memory gate is the workload check: a "fits memory" claim in this chapter means single-request residency unless a host or card count is given.'
root_cause: The single-request residency check and the workload memory gate were collapsed in the mini-case conclusion.
correction: Reword to: 'single-request memory passes, but the memory gate fails for one host because workload KV residency does not; throughput remains open as a measured SLO gate.'
acceptance_test: The mini-case no longer says 'memory passes' for candidate (a) while also saying 'workload KV residency does not', unless 'memory passes' is explicitly qualified as single-request only.

quoted_clause: All three candidates carry forward into the evaluation chapters (Chs 14–16) as conditional finalists — the §12.1 definition: advanced to evaluation with a named open gate, not promoted as passed — each with a distinct test plan: (a) and (b) carry the throughput gate open (and the TTFT SLO unmeasured), (c) carries the quality gate open, and no candidate is excluded pre-measurement.
observed: Candidate (a) is introduced as a 'single 8×H100 host', but §12.3 says that single host is not memory-feasible for the workload and is 'memory-feasible only as a multi-host deployment'. If the candidate is truly a single host, its memory gate fails and it should not be a conditional finalist with only throughput open. If the candidate is the replicated host class, its name and scope should say so.
evidence: §12.3: 'Candidate (a) is therefore memory-feasible only as a multi-host deployment, not as one host.' Table 12-1 marks (a) memory '✗ workload (~6 hosts avg / ~21 peak)' while still calling it a conditional finalist.
root_cause: Candidate (a) is ambiguously scoped as both a single-host latency baseline and a workload-capacity candidate, causing the gate status to omit a failed memory gate.
correction: Rename candidate (a) to '8×H100 host class with prefix caching (single-host latency baseline; replicated for capacity)' or explicitly state that the single-host layout fails the memory gate and the advanced candidate is the replicated host class. Then list the open/failed gates consistently.
acceptance_test: Every candidate called a conditional finalist has no un-named failed gate; candidate (a)'s scope is explicit as either single-host (and therefore not a workload finalist) or host-class (and named as such).

quoted_clause: If the architecture calls for data-parallel training of a 70B FP16 model across 8 nodes (an eight-rank DP group, e.g. one rank per node), the all-reduce bandwidth dictates whether the nodes are connected by InfiniBand, 200 GbE, or even 100 GbE. If the budget can accommodate NVLink‑equipped hosts (GPUs connected on‑node), the ratios are: an ideal ring time about 1/11th the assumed InfiniBand case and about 1/180th the assumed RoCE case (§9.3), for a single-host eight-rank collective against a cross-host one
observed: The first sentence describes an eight-node DP group with one rank per node, whose all-reduce is necessarily inter-node. The following ratios, however, compare a single-host eight-rank NVLink collective with a cross-host collective. As written, the paragraph can be read as applying the NVLink 1/11 and 1/180 ratios to the eight-node DP job.
evidence: Later in the same section: 'For the eight-node DP job the all-reduce is necessarily inter-node, so compare InfiniBand with Ethernet only for that portion.'
root_cause: Two different topologies (8-node DP vs 8-GPU single-host) are introduced in one paragraph without a clear case boundary.
correction: Separate the cases: (1) for 8-node DP, compare inter-node fabrics (InfiniBand vs Ethernet); (2) for an 8-rank collective inside one NVLink host, the 1/11 and 1/180 ratios apply relative to cross-host effective fabric cases. State that the NVLink ratios do not apply to the 8-node DP all-reduce.
acceptance_test: A reader cannot infer that an eight-node DP all-reduce uses the single-host NVLink 1/11 or 1/180 ratios; the two topologies are explicitly distinguished.

page_hint: Chapter 10, §2 Mental Model, resource triangle paragraph
quoted_clause: When the model is too big to replicate, TP wins over DP.
observed: This is overgeneralized. If the model is too big to replicate on one GPU but also too big for one node, TP alone may not be sufficient; PP or TP+PP may be required.
evidence: Same chapter, §6: 'fits one node → TP among its GPUs; spans nodes → PP across them, with TP inside each node.'
root_cause: The sentence omits the node-boundary case.
correction: Change to: 'When the model is too big to replicate, TP is preferred over plain DP if it fits the node; if it also exceeds the node, use TP+PP or PP.'
acceptance_test: The mental-model sentence acknowledges that TP may be insufficient when the model exceeds a node, consistent with §10.6.

page_hint: Chapter 10, §3 Worked Example, Data Parallelism paragraph
quoted_clause: a full-replica FP32 gradient alone is 1.6 TB, i.e. ~3.2 TB of ring traffic per rank, 7.1 s at 450 GB/s and 128 s at 25 GB/s
observed: The 3.2 TB figure is 2× the logical 1.6 TB gradient, which corresponds to the large-N limit of the ring send volume 2(N−1)/N × M. For N=8, the per-rank send volume would be 2.8 TB, not 3.2 TB. The sentence does not state the rank count or that this is a large-N approximation.
evidence: The chapter's own formula: per-rank send volume = 2(N−1)/N × M. For M=1.6 TB and N=8: 2×7/8×1.6 = 2.8 TB. As N→∞: 3.2 TB.
root_cause: The ring traffic was approximated by 2M without specifying N.
correction: Either state 'for a large DP group' before using ~3.2 TB, or choose an explicit N and use 2(N−1)/N × 1.6 TB (e.g., 2.8 TB for N=8).
acceptance_test: The quoted ring traffic matches the stated rank count, or the text explicitly labels 3.2 TB as a large-N approximation.

quoted_clause: Gate status is a three-value vocabulary — pass, fail (measured, below requirement), open (not yet measured)
observed: Later in the same chapter, analytical infeasibility is marked with ✗ before measurement, e.g., Table 12-1 marks candidate (a) memory as '✗ workload (~6 hosts avg / ~21 peak)' without a measurement. The defined 'fail' only covers measured failure.
evidence: Table 12-1: 'memory: ✓ residency 164 < 640 GB · ✗ workload (~6 hosts avg / ~21 peak)'.
root_cause: The gate vocabulary does not distinguish measured failure from analytical/screen failure.
correction: Define fail as 'measured or analytically infeasible under the stated assumptions', or introduce a separate 'screen fail' label and keep 'gate fail' for measured results.
acceptance_test: The gate vocabulary can consistently describe both measured failures and analytical infeasibility used in Tables 12-1/12-2.

quoted_clause: the ~2,472 figure is one GPU's share of the 70B's full-model FLOPs, i.e. a full-model-equivalent rate, never a per-GPU capability
observed: 2,472 is a token rate (tok/s), not a FLOP share. It is obtained by dividing one GPU's 35% MFU throughput by the full-model 2N FLOPs per token (140 GFLOP/token), not by taking a FLOP share.
evidence: 989 TFLOP/s × 0.35 = 346.15 TFLOP/s. 346.15 / 140 GFLOP/token ≈ 2,472 tok/s. The full-model 2N term for 70B is 140 GFLOP/token; the per-GPU TP=8 2N term is 17.5 GFLOP/token.
root_cause: The sentence describes a derived token rate as if it were a FLOP allocation.
correction: Reword to: 'the ~2,472 tok/s figure is the rate obtained by applying one GPU's 35% MFU to the full-model 2N FLOPs (140 GFLOP/token); it is a full-model-equivalent single-GPU rate, not the TP=8 per-GPU capability.'
acceptance_test: The 2,472 quantity is explicitly identified as a token rate, and the FLOP basis (full-model 140 GFLOP/token) is stated.

page_hint: Chapter 13, §8 End-of-Chapter Mini-Case, fleet sizing paragraph
quoted_clause: At 78 hosts the average load is 100 ÷ 78 ≈ 1.28 rps per host against the 1.98 rps ceiling, so the 68% headroom plus the spare absorbs burst
observed: 1.28 / 1.98 ≈ 0.647, so the fleet uses about 65% of the full-utilization ceiling and has about 35% headroom to that ceiling, not 68% headroom.
root_cause: The percentage was mislabeled as headroom instead of utilization, or computed from a different denominator.
correction: Change to 'about 35% headroom to the full-utilization ceiling' or 'about 65% of the full-utilization ceiling is used'.
acceptance_test: The stated percentage matches 1 − (100/78)/(17/8.6), or is explicitly labeled as utilization rather than headroom.

page_hint: Chapter 10, §3 Worked Example, Data Parallelism paragraph
quoted_clause: per-rank send volume is nearly flat in replica count (2(N-1)/N × 280 GB is 280 GB at N=2, 490 GB at N=8, 551 GB at N=64)
observed: The listed values increase from 280 GB at N=2 to 490 GB at N=8, a 75% increase. 'Nearly flat' is only appropriate in the large-N asymptote, not across the small-N range shown.
root_cause: The wording generalizes the asymptotic behavior to the whole range.
correction: Change to 'approaches 560 GB as N grows, but rises substantially from N=2 to N=8' or 'is nearly flat only for large N'.
acceptance_test: The sentence does not call the N=2 to N=8 increase 'nearly flat' without qualifying the large-N scope.

quoted_clause: Moving up to cluster introduces: DP/PP/TP replicas (Ch10), P/D disaggregation (Ch 11), and interconnect budgeting (Ch9).
observed: DP is replication; PP and TP are partitioning strategies, not replicas. The shorthand 'DP/PP/TP replicas' is technically imprecise.
evidence: Ch 10 defines DP as replicating the model and TP/PP as splitting weights or layers.
root_cause: Compressed wording grouped partitioning strategies with replication.
correction: Change to 'DP replicas and PP/TP splits' or 'DP, PP, and TP strategies'.
acceptance_test: PP and TP are not called replicas in this sentence.

page_hint: Chapter 13, §3 Worked Example, Escalating paragraph, naive-screen parenthetical
quoted_clause: 50 × (17.5 ÷ 8.6 ≈ 2.03) ≈ 101.7 rps, exactly at the 100 rps demand with zero utilization headroom
observed: 101.7 rps is not exactly 100 rps; it is about 1.7% above the demand. The word 'exactly' overstates the arithmetic.
root_cause: Rhetorical 'exactly' was used for an approximate boundary.
correction: Change to 'at or slightly above the 100 rps demand' or 'within about 2% of the 100 rps demand'.
acceptance_test: The sentence no longer says the 101.7 rps capacity is exactly equal to the 100 rps demand.
